info.title: Evolus Integration API
info.description:
The Evolus Integration API lets your application create and operate agents, AI employees, knowledge bases, workflows and document extraction pipelines.

## Authentication

Every request must identify the target application with the `X-Application-Id` header (a GUID), except the OpenAI Compatible endpoints described below. Two authentication methods are supported:

| Method | Headers | Use case |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Application API Key** | `X-ApiKey` + `X-Application-Id` | Server-to-server integrations acting on behalf of the application. |
| **User API Key** | `X-User-ApiKey` + `X-Application-Id` | Calls performed as a specific user, with that user's permissions, scoped to the target application. |

Application API keys are created by your administrator in the Evolus portal under *Your company › For developers › Developer keys*. Personal User API keys are managed from your Profile (*Personal API keys*).

The **OpenAI Compatible** endpoints (`/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/models`) follow the OpenAI convention instead: send the Application API Key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>`, without `X-Application-Id` (the application comes from the key and from the `model`, formatted as `{applicationId}:{agentId}`). User API keys are not accepted there.

## Rate limits

Requests are rate limited per application. Calls made with an API key (application key, user key, or the Bearer key of the OpenAI Compatible endpoints) share the per-minute limit of the application's subscription plan when the plan sets one: **60 requests per minute** on the Developer plans. Otherwise the standard per-application limit applies. Over the limit the API answers `429 Too Many Requests` with a `Retry-After` header carrying the seconds to wait: a problem+json with `errorCode` `common.too_many_requests`, or an OpenAI-shaped `rate_limit_error` on the OpenAI Compatible endpoints. Wait the indicated time before retrying.

## Conventions

- Identifiers are GUIDs unless stated otherwise.
- Long-running operations (workflow executions, AskFile extractions, background ingestion) respond with correlation headers such as `X-Workflow-Execution-Id` or `X-AskFile-Audit-Id` that you can use to reconcile results delivered to your webhooks.
- Streaming endpoints use Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`). Lines starting with `:` are comments that keep an idle connection alive (e.g. `: keep-alive` while an agent works on its tools): they are not events, ignore them.
- Requests rejected for missing permissions return `403 Forbidden`; missing or invalid credentials return `401 Unauthorized`; exhausted LLM credits return `402 Payment Required`; too many requests return `429 Too Many Requests` (see *Rate limits*).

get.description: Retrieves all agents configured for the current application. The model of each agent is its `modelKey` (null = "Let Evolus decide"), with `modelDisplayName` and `modelState` (`ok`, `deprecated`, `not_in_catalog`: the model left the catalog and the agent must be reconfigured). The `avatarUrl` field, when present, is returned as a time-limited SAS URL ready to be displayed.

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

post.description: Creates a new agent with the given name, prompt, model configuration and optional tags. The target application is resolved from the `X-Application-Id` header first, then from the `applicationId` field in the request body; if neither is provided the request fails with `400 Bad Request`. The model is chosen by its KEY (`modelKey`, `author/model` or `own/<alias>`, as offered by `GET api/v1/ai/catalog`; omitted or null = "Let Evolus decide": the agent follows the platform default model), with optional `fallbackModelKeys`, `routerWebSearch` and `ocrModelKey`. The model key goes through the same checks as the catalog: unknown model `ai.model_not_found`, model outside the application's allow list `ai.model_not_allowed`, tier not in the plan `plan.feature_not_included` (402), data policy `ai.data_policy_no_route`; `ocrModelKey` must be usable by the application (`ocr_models.not_assigned`). The old model fields (`modelName`, `modelType`, `llmProviderId`, `routerProviderOrder`, `routerAllowFallbacks`, `routerFallbackModels`, `ocrModelName`) are no longer accepted: sending them answers `422 ai.legacy_model_fields`, which lists them and the replacing field. `isExtractor` = true marks a data extractor: an agent that extracts data from documents with an output structure, shown in the Data extractors section of the portal (it adds the system tag `evo:extractor` to `tags`; false removes it, omitted leaves `tags` as sent). Returns the newly created agent, whose read-only `isExtractor` reflects that tag.

Retrieves the agents of the current application published in the unified portal chat (`isChatVisible`). Returns presentation data only (`agentId`, `name`, `description`, `avatarUrl` as a time-limited SAS URL): no configuration details are exposed, so the endpoint is safe for chat-only users.

**User authentication required** — this operation does NOT accept the application API key (`X-ApiKey`): call it with a personal User API Key (`X-User-ApiKey` + `X-Application-Id`).

get.description: Retrieves a single agent by its `agentId` within the current application. The `avatarUrl` field, when present, is returned as a time-limited SAS URL. Returns `404 Not Found` if the agent does not exist.

put.description: Updates the configuration of an existing agent (name, description, prompt, model, tags and related options). PARTIAL update: an omitted key keeps its current value (the model included), a key sent as `null` clears that field (`name` and `prompt` cannot be null: `422`), a key with a value sets it. The model is its KEY (`modelKey`, `author/model` or `own/<alias>`): omitted = unchanged, `null` = "Let Evolus decide" (the platform default model); `fallbackModelKeys` (omitted = unchanged, null or `[]` = none) and `ocrModelKey` (null = OCR off) follow the same rule, and `routerWebSearch` turns the native web search on or off. A few fields keep their current value even when sent as null: `webSearchType`, `serviceType`, `modelParameters` (send `{}` to clear), `agentProfile`, `tags` (send `[]` to clear), `mcpServers`, `costGroupId` (send the all-zero GUID to unassign) and the boolean switches. A changed `costGroupId` must be a user group of the agent's own application: a group of another application answers like one that does not exist (`404 Not Found`, `common.not_found`). `modelParameters` keys must be declared by the target model (the `parameterDefinitions` of the model, the `supported_parameters` of a router model) and never routing options (`provider`, `models`, `plugins`...): an undeclared key is rejected with `422` (`errors.modelParameters = [not_allowed]`, the offending keys are listed in `detail`) instead of being silently dropped; a model without a declared schema accepts any key. When the update CHANGES the model key, or adds a fallback, it goes through the same checks as the catalog (`ai.model_not_found`, `ai.model_not_allowed`, `plan.feature_not_included` for the tier, `ai.data_policy_no_route`, deprecated `409`); a changed `ocrModelKey` must be usable by the application (`422` `ocr_models.not_assigned`). The old model fields (`modelName`, `modelType`, `llmProviderId`, `routerProviderOrder`, `routerAllowFallbacks`, `routerFallbackModels`, `ocrModelName`) are no longer accepted: sending them answers `422 ai.legacy_model_fields`. `isExtractor` = true marks a data extractor: an agent that extracts data from documents with an output structure, shown in the Data extractors section of the portal (it adds the system tag `evo:extractor`); false removes the tag; the other tags are untouched, and omitted or null keeps the current value. Sent together with `tags`, it applies to the new list. Returns the updated agent.

post.description: Creates a copy of the agent (data extractors included: they are the same entity and keep their reserved tag) in the same application, named "… (copia)" (with a progressive number when that name is taken). The copy carries the full configuration (prompt, model key and fallback keys, parameters, profile, tags, switches) and the attached capabilities — functions, web APIs, MCP servers (with their additional prompts and disabled tools), skills, helper agents and, for restricted agents, the access grants. Knowledge documents, memories, conversations, the avatar and the cost group are NOT carried over. Counts toward the plan agent limit and re-checks the model like a regular creation (the same checks as the catalog: allow list, plan tier, data policy) and the OCR model must be usable by the application (`422` `ocr_models.not_assigned`). Returns the created copy, or `404 Not Found` if the agent does not exist.

post.description: Assigns the MCP (Model Context Protocol) server identified by `mcpServerId` to the agent, exposing the server's tools to the agent during conversations. The server must belong to an MCP collection of the agent's own application: an id of another application answers like one that does not exist (`404 Not Found`, `mcp.server_not_found`). post.description: Sends a question to the agent and waits for the complete answer, returned with `conversationId`, `title` and `citations`. `totalTokenCount` IS PLATFORM-STAFF-ONLY and comes back `null` to every other caller: LLM tokens are the platform's own internals, the unit consumption is measured in is credits. Pass an existing `conversationId` to continue a conversation, and a `fileId` from the upload endpoint to attach a file to the question. A `conversationId` that exists but does not belong to the caller (a conversation of another application, of another user, or of a user when calling with an application key) answers `404 Not Found` (`common.not_found`) and nothing is read from or written to it; an id that does not exist starts a new conversation with that id. A `fileId` uploaded in another application, or already used in another conversation, is ignored as if it did not exist. End-user credentials for the agent's MCP servers travel in the optional `mcpUserTokens` map (slot name -> verbatim header value): each value reaches ONLY the MCP servers declaring that slot in their `auth` block, and a server whose slot is missing is not connected at all. Slots prefixed with `evolus.` are reserved for the backend and are silently discarded; `evolus.user_token` is filled server-side with the caller's bearer JWT. The legacy `X-MCP-Authorization` header still works and lands on the `default` slot. When the agent has the working-area file tools enabled it can deliver a file of its working area as its answer (`SendFileToOutputAsync`): `answer` is then the content of that file, exactly, and the conversation stores the same text. A question needs text: when `content` is missing, empty or only whitespace and no `fileId` is sent, the request answers `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`common.validation`, field `content`, reason `required`) and the agent is not called. The request fails with `402 Payment Required` (`credits.llm_exhausted` when the balance is gone, `credits.subscription_inactive` when the remaining credits are frozen because the subscription is no longer active) when the application has no spendable LLM credits, unless the agent runs on one of the application's own models (connected in "Your models"): the agent's model does not spend LLM credits, so an empty balance does not stop the request.

post.summary: Ask an agent a question within a project
post.description: Sends a question to the agent scoped to the project identified by `projectId`, so the project's memories and documents are included in the agent's knowledge. Behaves like the standard ask endpoint: supports `conversationId` for continuity, `fileId` for attachments and the `mcpUserTokens` slot map (with the legacy `X-MCP-Authorization` header mapped to the `default` slot) for per-server MCP passthrough credentials. Returns the complete answer with conversation metadata. A `conversationId` that exists but does not belong to the caller answers `404 Not Found` (`common.not_found`), as on the standard ask endpoint. `totalTokenCount` IS PLATFORM-STAFF-ONLY and comes back `null` to every other caller. When the agent has the working-area file tools enabled it can deliver a file of its working area as its answer (`SendFileToOutputAsync`): `answer` is then the content of that file, exactly, and the conversation stores the same text. A question needs text: when `content` is missing, empty or only whitespace and no `fileId` is sent, the request answers `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`common.validation`, field `content`, reason `required`) and the agent is not called. The request fails with `402 Payment Required` (`credits.llm_exhausted` when the balance is gone, `credits.subscription_inactive` when the remaining credits are frozen because the subscription is no longer active) when the application has no spendable LLM credits, unless the agent runs on one of the application's own models (connected in "Your models"): the agent's model does not spend LLM credits, so an empty balance does not stop the request.

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

post.summary: Ask an agent a question with a streaming response
post.description: Sends a question to the agent and streams the answer as Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`). Each event carries a JSON chunk with incremental `content`; the final chunk has `isComplete: true` and includes `conversationId`, `title` and `citations`. `totalTokenCount` IS PLATFORM-STAFF-ONLY: every other caller simply does not receive the field. Supports the same request options as the synchronous ask endpoint (`conversationId`, `fileId`, `mcpUserTokens` slot map and the legacy `X-MCP-Authorization` header); a `conversationId` that exists but does not belong to the caller answers `404 Not Found` (`common.not_found`) before the stream opens. While the answer is being prepared, the stream also carries SSE comment lines (`: keep-alive`, every 15 seconds by default) so that clients and proxies do not close a connection that looks idle while the agent works on its tools: they are not events and SSE clients ignore them. When the agent has the working-area file tools enabled it can deliver a file of its working area as its answer (`SendFileToOutputAsync`): since the file replaces any text of the turn, the answer is not streamed while it is written but arrives in ONE `content` chunk before the final chunk (the delivered file, or the agent's text if it delivered none). A question needs text: when `content` is missing, empty or only whitespace and no `fileId` is sent, the request answers `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`common.validation`, field `content`, reason `required`) before the stream opens and the agent is not called. The request fails with `402 Payment Required` (`credits.llm_exhausted` when the balance is gone, `credits.subscription_inactive` when the remaining credits are frozen because the subscription is no longer active) when the application has no spendable LLM credits, unless the agent runs on one of the application's own models (connected in "Your models"): the agent's model does not spend LLM credits, so an empty balance does not stop the request.

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

post.summary: Ask an agent a question within a project with a streaming response
post.description: Sends a question to the agent scoped to the project identified by `projectId` and streams the answer as Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`). When the agent has the working-area file tools enabled it can deliver a file of its working area as its answer (`SendFileToOutputAsync`): since the file replaces any text of the turn, the answer is not streamed while it is written but arrives in ONE `content` chunk before the final chunk (the delivered file, or the agent's text if it delivered none). post.description: Uploads a file via `multipart/form-data` (single `file` field) to be used as an attachment in conversations with the agent. The file is stored temporarily and the returned `fileId` can be passed in subsequent ask requests; use the optional `conversationId` query parameter to associate the file with an existing conversation of the caller. A conversation that exists but belongs to someone else (another person, another application, or a person's conversation when calling with an application key) answers `404 Not Found` (`common.not_found`) like the ask routes, and nothing is uploaded.

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

delete.description: Deletes a previously uploaded temporary conversation file identified by `fileId`. Returns `204 No Content` on success.

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

get.description: Retrieves all conversations held with the agent identified by `agentId`. Returns conversation metadata only, without the full message history. `tokens` is platform-staff-only: it is `null` for every other caller.

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

get.description: Retrieves the conversation identified by `conversationId`, including its full message history and responses. What the conversation consumed is reported by `consumption`, aggregated from the usage entries of the conversation and of every sub-agent it delegated to, at any depth: `credits` (credits charged to the plan — the unit consumption is measured in; `null` until the credit job has processed at least one entry, and still partial while `pendingEntries` is greater than zero) and `pendingEntries` (AI calls not priced yet; `0` means `credits` is final). `consumption` is `null` while the conversation has no usage entries. THE OTHER CONSUMPTION FIELDS ARE PLATFORM-STAFF-ONLY and come back `null` to every other caller, because they are the platform's own internals: `consumption.costUsd` (raw provider cost), the `consumption` breakdown `llmTokens`/`ocrPages`/`embeddingTokens`/`speechToTextSeconds`/`entries` and the token counts (`tokens` on the conversation and `totalTokenCount` on each response).

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

get.description: Retrieves all subagent assignments configured on the orchestrator agent identified by `agentId`, including each subagent's name and prompt description.

post.description: Assigns the agent identified by `subAgentId` as a subagent of the orchestrator agent, with a `subAgentName` and an optional `subAgentPromptDescription` that tells the orchestrator when to delegate to it. The subagent must belong to the orchestrator's own application, not even another application of the same organization: an id of another application answers like one that does not exist (`404 Not Found`, `agents.not_found`). Returns the created subagent assignment.

delete.description: Removes a subagent assignment from the orchestrator agent by its `subAgentName` instead of its ID. Intended for ClaudeSdk orchestrator agents, where subagents are referenced by name. Returns `204 No Content` on success.

The memory must belong to the agent's own application: an id of another application answers like one that does not exist (`404 Not Found`, `memories.not_found`).

post.summary: Ensure the agent's personal knowledge memory
post.description: Returns the agent's personal knowledge memory of the requested `type` (flagged with `isKnowledge`), creating it with the platform defaults and linking it to the agent when missing. An agent can own one personal library per type: `Rag` (default, semantic search) and `Blob` ("simple memory", whole markdown files). Idempotent. Requires the app.memories:create permission.

get.description:
Returns the details of a single AI employee, including its container status and configuration metadata. Returns `404` if the employee does not exist or belongs to another application: the two cases get the same response.

**User authentication required** — this operation does NOT accept the application API key (`X-ApiKey`): call it with a personal User API Key (`X-User-ApiKey` + `X-Application-Id`).

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

get.description: Returns all AI employees visible to the caller, filtered by the active application. Use the returned `id` values as the `employeeId` path parameter required by every other operation.

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

get.description: Returns the runtime status of an AI employee: container state, health-check result and the number of active tasks. Useful for checking availability before creating tasks or starting a chat. `mcp_connectors` lists the external MCP connectors the employee left out because they failed at startup and is retrying in the background; it is absent on employees running an older image.

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

get.description: Returns the paginated tasks of an employee as `{ items, total, limit, offset }`. Each item carries `credits` (charged consumption, markup included, 0 until the orchestrator flushes it) and, for superadmins only, `costUsd`. Filter with `status` (`todo`, `in_progress`, `pending`, `completed`, `failed`), `assigned_worker` and `source_type` (exact match; the special value `action` matches every scheduled-action task, whose source_type is `action:<slug>`). Free-text filters on title+description, case-insensitive substring: `q` keeps only matching tasks, `exclude` hides matching tasks; they compose. Filter by creation time with `created_from`/`created_to` (inclusive bounds, format `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`, same clock as the stored `created_at`). Page with `limit` (default 50) and `offset` (default 0).

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

post.description: Creates a new task for the employee to execute and returns it with its assigned `id`. Provide `title` (required) and optionally `description`, `assigned_worker` and `priority` (1 = highest, 5 = lowest); pending tasks are picked up by the task runner in priority order. To attach files, upload them first via the task attachments endpoint and pass the returned ids in `attachment_ids`: the files are copied into the task folder on creation (`422` if an id has expired). A task created by an authenticated user carries that user's identity, so the run can use their per-person connectors; created with an API key the task stays anonymous.

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

post.description: Uploads one or more files via `multipart/form-data` (repeated `files` field, max 50MB each) to be attached to a task. Returns the `attachment_id` list to reference in the `attachment_ids` field when creating the task. Staged files not referenced by a task are retained for 72 hours.

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

get.description: Returns a single task by id (`status`, `assigned_worker`, `process_id`, timing and error fields) proxying the native GET of the upstream orchestrator; `404` if the task does not exist. Works for tasks in any state, including those still in `todo`. The result payload is not on the task record: use the task callback/webhook, or the `/result` endpoint to recover it.

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

put.description: Partially updates a task identified by `taskId`; only the provided fields are modified. Updatable fields: `title`, `description`, `status`, `assigned_worker`, `priority`, `pending_reason`, `pending_type`, `due_date`, `source_type`, `source_ref`, `is_passive`, `is_long_running`, `is_working` and `completion_condition`. Returns the updated task.

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

delete.description: Permanently deletes a task and its activity log from the employee. This action cannot be undone.

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

get.description: Returns ONLY the final JSON payload produced by the worker for the task — the same body delivered by the task callback — extracted from the task activity log: the last envelope the worker either wrote with the `Write` tool or printed in the log (`cat` via Bash, or `Read`). Returns `404 {status:no_result_yet}` when the task has not produced a result yet (still queued, running, or failed before writing one). The primary delivery channel remains the callback: use this endpoint to recover the payload when the callback was not delivered.

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

get.description: Returns the full NDJSON activity log of a task, one JSON event per line: user prompts, assistant responses (with the optional `message.thinking` reasoning text plus `text` and `tool_use` content blocks) and the final result with cost and usage. Pass `offset` (byte offset, `0` on the first call) to read INCREMENTALLY instead: the response becomes `application/json` `{ "entries": [...], "next_offset": int, "eof": bool }` with the parsed events written after that offset — send `next_offset` back on the next poll and stop when `eof` is true. A log not written yet answers `{ "entries": [], "next_offset": <offset>, "eof": false }` instead of `404`, so polling can start before the first event. Without `offset` the historical NDJSON body is returned. `/activity/stream` remains available to follow the log over SSE.

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

get.description: Streams the worker activity of a task in real time over Server-Sent Events (`text/event-stream`). post.summary: Upload a document to a memory
post.description: Uploads a file (`multipart/form-data`) and ingests it into the memory's RAG vector store, by default as a background job (`backgroundIngestion=true`) with `Classic` chunking and `MultiVector` indexing. The file format is validated up front against the list returned by `GET /api/v1/memories/document-formats`: an unsupported format is rejected with `422 Unprocessable Entity` instead of being accepted and failing minutes later (the check is skipped for `chunkingStrategy=WorkflowBased`, where the workflow reads the original file). Files above the configured size limit are rejected with `413 Payload Too Large`. Ingestion can be tuned via query parameters such as `chunkingStrategy`, `indexingStrategy`, `language` (default `it`), `augmentation`, `rephrasings`, `implicitQuestions` and `ocrModelKey` (the key of the OCR model, `author/model`; an OCR model that exists but is neither global nor assigned to the memory's application is rejected with `422` `ocr_models.not_assigned` before the file is stored; the old `ocrModelName` parameter is no longer accepted: `422 ai.legacy_model_fields`). On a `Blob` memory ("simple memory") there is no ingestion pipeline: only textual formats (`.md`, `.txt`, `.json`, `.csv`, `.js`) up to `AppSettings:BlobMemoryMaxFileSizeMb` (default 1 MB) are accepted, the pipeline query parameters are ignored and the document is returned already `Indexed`. `chunkingWorkflowId` and `augmentationWorkflowId` must be workflows of the memory's own application or workflows the platform published as global for that purpose (`Chunking` / `Augmentation`): any other id, another application's included, is rejected before the file is stored with `404 Not Found` (`workflows.not_found`), as for a workflow that does not exist. Indexing is billed in AI credits (embeddings): with `backgroundIngestion=false` an application without spendable credits gets `402 Payment Required` before the file is stored, while in background the document is accepted and the job moves it to `Failed` with the ingestion error `credits_exhausted` (or `subscription_inactive` when the balance is frozen by an inactive subscription): nothing is indexed and nothing is billed, and `retry-ingestion` re-queues it after the top-up. Returns the created `MemoryDocument` with `201 Created`.

post.description: OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint: point any OpenAI SDK at this server's `/v1` base URL, authenticate with `Authorization: Bearer <Application API Key>` and use `{applicationId}:{agentId}` as the `model` to chat with an Evolus agent. Supports `stream: true` (Server-Sent Events terminated by `data: [DONE]`); send the optional `X-Conversation-Id` request header to continue a server-side conversation (history is loaded from the conversation and only the last `user` message is processed), otherwise previous messages in the request are inlined as context and a new conversation is created. An `X-Conversation-Id` of a conversation that exists but does not belong to the key (a conversation of another application, or of a user) answers `404` with an OpenAI-shaped `invalid_request_error` (code `common.not_found`), also with `stream: true` (before the stream opens), and nothing is read from or written to it; an id that does not exist starts a new conversation with that id. The response always includes the `X-Conversation-Id` header so the conversation can be resumed in subsequent calls. Requests are rejected with `402` and an OpenAI-shaped `insufficient_quota` error when the application has no spendable LLM credits: code `credits.llm_exhausted` when the balance is gone, `credits.subscription_inactive` when the remaining credits are frozen because the subscription is no longer active. This check does not apply when the agent runs on one of the application's own models (connected in "Your models"): the agent's model does not spend LLM credits, so an empty balance does not stop the request. The last `user` message must carry a non-empty text `content`: otherwise the request answers `400` with an OpenAI-shaped `invalid_request_error` (`param`: `messages`) and the agent is not called. An AI block (`LlmCall`, or `If`/`Switch`/`ForEach` in `llm` mode) whose `stepConfigJson` has no `modelKey` runs on the platform default model, chosen automatically at every run: the save answers `422` on `modelKey` (`llm.modelKey`) when that default is not available for the application, and on `modelParameters` when they are sent without a model. The old model keys (`modelName`, `modelType`, `llmProviderId`, `providerOrder`, `allowFallbacks`, `fallbackModels`, `ocrModelName`) are no longer accepted, in the body or inside `stepConfigJson`: sending them answers `422 ai.legacy_model_fields`. References to the output of another step are written `{{step:<stepId>}}` (or `{{step:<stepId>.path}}`): the legacy numbered form `{{step_N_output}}` is still read, but on save it is converted to `{{step:<stepId>}}` with the current step order, because the order changes when the blocks are moved. A sent `stepConfigJson` replaces the saved one, but for an AI block that keeps its type an omitted `modelKey` keeps the saved model keys, while `modelKey: null` goes back to the platform default model. post.description: Queues an asynchronous execution of the workflow with optional text input and/or file attachments. A workflow that is turned off (`isActive` false) is not run: the call responds `409 Conflict` immediately, no execution is created and nothing is queued. The only exception is the manual test from the portal: the query parameter `manualTest=true` runs the workflow even when it is off, and it is honoured ONLY for a person signed in interactively with their own Keycloak token; with an application API key or a user API key (MCP included) it is ignored. A manual test run carries `isManualTest: true` on the execution. A workflow with no steps to run (no steps at all, or only steps that belong to a loop body) can never succeed: the call responds `409 Conflict` immediately, manual test included, no execution is created and nothing is queued. Send `multipart/form-data` with an `input` field for text plus one or more file parts, or a raw text body. With several file parts the behaviour depends on the workflow `multiFileMode`: `PerFile` (0, default) runs the whole pipeline once per file (same text input, one file each, N results and N webhook deliveries), `Combined` (1) runs it once with all the files together (the OCR step concatenates their texts, one result and one delivery). Optional form fields `callbackUrl`, `callbackMethod` (POST|PUT|PATCH, default POST), `callbackApiKey` and `callbackApiKeyName` (default `x-api-key`) override, for this execution only, the destination of every Webhook step: the URL, the HTTP method and the API key of the override replace the configured catalog webhook or free URL, also for a step configured as 'Call an endpoint (API)', whose own headers are then NOT sent (they belong to the configured destination); body, send format and response type stay those of the step. The override reaches the workflows called by 'Call a workflow' steps too, waited for or queued, at every nesting level (400 if neither the workflow nor the workflows it calls have a Webhook step; the override requires `callbackUrl` and is only available with multipart form requests; `422 Unprocessable Entity` with `network.address_not_allowed` if `callbackUrl` points to an internal, private or reserved address, which the platform never calls). The optional form field `parameters` carries the EXECUTION PARAMETERS as a flat JSON object (also multipart only): a string for each parameter declared as `type: "string"` and a JSON array of strings for each `type: "list"` one, for example `parameters={"target_language":"German"}`. Values are validated against the declaration returned by `GET /workflows/{workflowId}` BEFORE the job is queued, so nothing is charged when they are wrong: an undeclared key, a type other than the declared one, a missing required parameter, a value outside `allowedValues` or a breach of the limits (20 parameters, 500 characters per value, 50 items per list) all respond `400 Bad Request`. Declared defaults are applied to the parameters that are absent, and the resolved set is stored on the execution and reused as-is by automatic retries. Never send secrets as parameters: they are stored and shown in clear in the execution detail. Responds `202 Accepted` with `{ jobId, executionId, enqueuedAt, traceId }` and the `X-Workflow-Execution-Id` header; the same execution ID, together with the `X-Workflow-Audit-Id` of the run audit, is forwarded to any webhook steps so results can be correlated. Both headers travel on EVERY delivery of the execution — the audit is created once per run and its ID is repeated identical on each delivery, the iterations of a 'Repeat for each item' block included — so a receiver can group the deliveries of one run without depending on which one arrived first. Every delivery also carries `X-Workflow-Root-Execution-Id`: the execution ID returned by this call, also on the deliveries of the workflows started by 'Call a workflow' steps (which carry their own execution in `X-Workflow-Execution-Id` and their own audit), so the deliveries of a called workflow can be matched to the run that was started. Every `file` part a webhook step delivers carries the part header `X-File-Label` when the document has a label: the 'AI tool' step in translate mode labels its output with the TARGET LANGUAGE (and names the file after it, `report-german.docx`), so a delivery carrying several translations of the same document can be attributed without parsing file names. A step placed after a 'Repeat for each item' block receives every document its body produced, in item order and, within an item, in step order.

X-Workflow-Execution-Id.description: Stable Id of the WorkflowExecution record (whole run). Returned synchronously to the caller and replayed in every webhook step header X-Workflow-Execution-Id of the same execution.

get.description: Returns a paginated list of executions for the workflow, ordered by most recent first. Use the `page` and `pageSize` query parameters to paginate (defaults: `1` and `20`). `error` is set only on `Failed` executions. `totalTokenCount` is platform-staff-only and carries the same value as on the execution detail: it is `null` for every other caller. Per-run consumption (`consumption`) is only returned by the execution detail endpoint.

500.description: Unexpected error (standard problem+json with errorCode and traceId)

get.description: Returns the details and result of a single workflow execution, including the `parameters` the run started with (declared defaults included) for troubleshooting. The `executionId` is the value returned by the execute endpoint and in the `X-Workflow-Execution-Id` header; responds `404 Not Found` if the execution does not exist or does not belong to the workflow. `error` is set only on `Failed` executions: an automatic retry reuses the same execution and clears the error of the failed attempt. Runs started by a 'Call workflow' step carry the parent/root linking fields (`parentExecutionId`, `parentWorkflowId`, `parentStepId`, `parentIterationIndex`, `rootExecutionId`), and `childExecutions` lists the runs this execution started. What the run consumed is reported by `consumption`, aggregated from the usage entries of the run: `credits` (credits charged to the plan — the unit consumption is measured in; `null` until the credit job has processed at least one entry, and still partial while `pendingEntries` is greater than zero) and `pendingEntries` (AI calls of the run not priced yet; `0` means `credits` is final). THE OTHER CONSUMPTION FIELDS ARE PLATFORM-STAFF-ONLY and come back `null` to every other caller — they are the platform's own internals: `totalTokenCount` (LLM tokens of the run, aligned with `consumption.llmTokens` and therefore counting every automatic retry attempt; without usage entries it is the engine count of the last attempt), `consumption.costUsd` (raw provider cost) and the `consumption` breakdown `llmTokens`/`ocrPages`/`embeddingTokens`/`speechToTextSeconds`/`entries`. Consumption covers THIS execution only: runs started by a 'Call workflow' step report their own on their own detail.

put.description: Sets, replaces, pauses or removes the workflow's scheduled (cron) trigger in one full-replace call. `cron` accepts 5 fields or 6 with seconds, read in the IANA `timeZone` (default UTC); occurrences must be at least 30 seconds apart. An empty `cron` removes the schedule. With `paused` true the scheduler skips the workflow and, on resume, missed runs are NOT recovered: the next occurrence is always computed from now. The schedule can be set while the workflow is turned off too: scheduled runs start only while it is on, and when it is turned back on the next occurrence is computed from that moment (a time already passed never starts a run). The optional `input` is the text fed to every scheduled run. Scheduled runs consume credits like any other execution.

get.description: Validates a cron expression (5 fields, or 6 with seconds) against the platform rules and returns the next 5 occurrences (UTC), the minimum observed interval in seconds and whether the under-one-hour LLM cost warning applies. Purely informational: nothing is saved.

title.description: Short English description (not the end-user message)

errorCode.description: Stable machine key '<domain>.<reason>' from the error catalog

traceId.description: W3C trace id (32 hex) for support/observability correlation

params.description: Values referenced by the localized message (declared per errorCode in the catalog)

errors.description: Validation only: field name → reason codes (required, invalid_format, max_length, ...)

EvolusProblemDetails.description: Standard Evolus error contract (RFC 9457 extended). errorCode is a stable machine key from the error catalog (error-catalog.json); traceId correlates the error with server-side traces and logs; params carries the values referenced by the localized message; errors (validation only) maps each invalid field to its reason codes.

ApiKey.description: API Key for external application access. Must be used together with X-Application-Id header.
ApiKey.name: X-ApiKey

ApplicationId.description: Application ID (GUID) associated with the API Key.
ApplicationId.name: X-Application-Id

UserApiKey.description: Personal user API key (GUID). Authenticates as the owning user via UserApiKeyAuthMiddleware. Optionally combine with X-Application-Id to scope to a specific application.
UserApiKey.name: X-User-ApiKey

OpenAiBearer.description: Application API key sent as `Authorization: Bearer <Application API Key>`. Accepted only by the OpenAI-compatible `/v1` endpoints, which take the application from the key itself (or from the `model`): no `X-Application-Id` header is needed.
